verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य सात्वतं युद्धदुर्मदम्। क्रोधाद्भूरिश्रवा राजन् सहसा समुपाद्रवत्॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Beholding that warrior indomitable in battle, that scion of the Sini race rush furiously to battle, o king, Bhurisravas, inflamed with wrath, assailed him.

verses.sanskrit: तमब्रवीन्महाराज कौरव्यः शिनिपुङ्गवम्। अद्य प्राप्तोऽसि दिष्ट्या मे चक्षुर्विषयमित्युत॥२॥
verses.english: Then, O mighty monarch, that foremost of the Kurus (Bhurisravas) addressing Sini's grandson thus spoke-"By good luck it is that you have today come within the range of my sight;

verses.sanskrit: चिराभिलषितं काममहं प्राप्स्यामि संयुगे। न हि मे मोक्ष्यसे जीवन् यदि नोत्सृजसे रणम्॥३॥
verses.english: Today, I shall realise in battle my longcherish I hope; you shall not escape me alive if indeed you do not fly away from the battle.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य त्वां समरे हत्वा नित्यं शूराभिमानिनम्। नंदयिष्यामि दाशार्ह कुरुराजं सुयोधनम्॥४॥
अद्य मद्बाणनिर्दग्धं पतितं धरणीतले। द्रक्ष्यतस्त्वां रणे वीरौ सहितौ केशवार्जुनौ॥५॥
अद्य धर्मसुतो राजा श्रुत्वा त्वां निहतं मया। सव्रीडो भविता सद्यो येनासीह प्रवेशितः॥६॥
अद्य मे विक्रमं पार्थो विशास्यति धनञ्जयः। त्वथि भूमौ विनिहते शयाने रुधिरोक्षिते॥७॥
चिराभिलषितो ह्येष त्वया सह समागमः। पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे शक्रस्य बलिना यथा ॥८॥
verses.english: This encounter with you has long been desired by me, like that desired by Shakra with Bali, in the battle between the Gods and the Asuras in days gone by.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य युद्धं महाघोरं तव दास्यामि सात्वत। ततो ज्ञास्यसि तत्त्वेन मद्वीर्यबलपौरुषम्॥९॥
verses.english: Today, O descendant of the Satvata race, I shall fight a terrible fight with you, whence you shall know my great mighty and manliness.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य संयमनीं याता मया त्वं निहतो रणे। यथा रामानुजेनाजौ रावणिर्लक्ष्मणेन ह॥१०॥
अद्य कृष्णश्च पार्थश्च धर्मराजश्च माधव। हते त्वयि निरुत्साहा रणं त्यक्ष्यन्त्यसंशयम्॥११॥
verses.english: Today Krishna, Partha and the virtuous king Yudhishthira, O Madhava, will abandon fighting and became despondent, consequence of your slaughter.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य तेऽपचितिं कृत्वा शितैर्माधव सायकैः। तत्स्त्रियो नन्दयिष्यामि ये त्वया निहता रणे॥१२॥
मच्चक्षुर्विषयं प्राप्तो न त्वं माधव मोक्ष्यसे। सिंहस्य विषयं प्राप्तो यथा क्षुद्रमृगस्तथा॥१३॥
युयुधानस्तु तं राजन्प्रत्युवाच हसन्निव। कौरवेय न संत्रासो विद्यते मम संयुगे॥१४॥
नाहं भीषयितुं शक्यो वाङ्मात्रेण तु केवलम्। स मां निहन्यात्संग्रामे यो मां कुर्यान्निरायुधम्॥१५॥
verses.english: I am not to be terrified by empty words. He will slay me in battle who will be competent to deprive me of my weapons.

verses.sanskrit: समास्तु शाश्वतीर्हन्याद्यो मां हन्याद्धि संयुगे। किं वृथोक्तेन बहुना कर्मणा तत्समाचर ॥१६॥
verses.english: He that will slay me in battle will ever be victorious. What is the use of vain boasts. Achieve in deeds what you say in words.

verses.sanskrit: शारदस्येव मेघस्य गर्जितं निष्फलं हि ते। श्रुत्वा त्वद्गर्जितं वीर हास्यं हि मम जायते॥१७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: शाश्वतीः समाः सर्वकालम् । तुरवधारणे नित्यमेव असौ हन्यात् । जय एव तस्येत्यर्थः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: चिरकालेप्सितं लोके युद्धमद्यास्तु कौरव। त्वरते मे मतिस्तात तव युद्धाभिकांक्षिणी॥१८॥
verses.english: O Kaurava, let the encounter which you looked so eargrly for, today take place; O sire, my heart that longs for the combat with you, cannot tolerate any more delay.

verses.sanskrit: नाहत्वाऽहं निवर्तिष्ये त्वामद्य पुरुषाधम। अन्योन्यं तौ तथा वाग्भिस्तक्षन्तौ नरपुङ्गवौ॥१९॥
verses.english: O wretch, I shall not abstain from the fight today without having slain you in battle.” Thus those two foremost of men, stirring each other with their biting words.

verses.sanskrit: जिघांसू परमक्रुद्धावभिजघ्नतुराहवे। समेतौ तौ महेष्वासौ शुष्मिणौ स्पर्धिनौ रणे॥२०॥
verses.english: And waxing wroth and desirous of slaying each other in battle began to smite each other. Then those two mighty bow-men both boastful of their prowess and both challenging each other.

verses.sanskrit: द्विरदाविव संक्रुद्धौ वासितार्थे मदोत्कटौ। भूरिश्रवाः सात्यकिश्च ववर्षतुररिन्दमौ॥२१॥
verses.english: Appeared like two infuriate elephants encounter each other, with a desire to consort with a she-elephant. Then those two subduers of foes, Bhurisravas and Satyaki began to pour.

verses.sanskrit: शरवर्षाणि घोराणि मेघाविव परस्परम्। सौमदत्तिस्तु शैनेयं प्रच्छाद्येषुभिराशुगैः॥२२॥
verses.english: On each other, dreadful showers of arrows like two mighty-clouds. Covering Sini's grandson with swift-coursing arrows, Somadatta's son.

verses.sanskrit: जिघांसुर्भरतश्रेष्ठ विव्याध निशितैः शरैः। दशभिः सात्यकिं विद्ध्वा सौमदत्तिरथापरान्॥२३॥
verses.english: O foremost of the Bharatas, desirous of slaying the former, pierced him with sharp arrows. Having pierced Satyaki then with ten arrows, Somadatta's son.

verses.sanskrit: मुमोच निशितान्बाणान् जिघांसुः शिनिपुङ्गवम्। तानस्य विशिखांस्तीक्ष्णानन्तरिक्षे विशांपते॥२४॥
verses.english: Out of a desire for slaying that illustrious scion of the Sini race, sped other sharp shafts at him. Then, O ruler of men, Satyaki with the illusion of his weapons devoured up all those up all those arrows, O lord, when they were ranging through the skies and before they had even reached him (Satyaki). Then those two heroes began to pour upon one another their showers of weapons.

verses.sanskrit: अप्राप्तानस्त्रमायाभिरग्रसत् सात्यकिः प्रभो। तौ पृथक् शस्त्रवर्षाभ्यामवर्षेतां परस्परम्॥२५॥
उत्तमाभिजनौ वीरौ कुरुवृष्णियशस्करौ। तौ नखैरिव शार्दूलौ दन्तैरिव महाद्विपौ॥२६॥
verses.english: Those two heroes, of noble extraction both enhancers of the fame of the Kurus and the Vrishnis respectively, began to fight with each other like two tigers fighting with claws or two elephants fighting with their tusks.

verses.sanskrit: रथशक्तिभिरन्योन्यं विशिखैश्चाप्यकृन्तताम्। निर्भिन्दंतौ हि गात्राणि विक्षरन्तौ च शोणितम्॥२७॥
verses.english: With lances and with darts and javelins they inflicted wounds on each other. They mangled their bodies and shed blood profusely.

verses.sanskrit: व्यष्टम्भयेतामन्योन्यं प्राणद्यूताभिदेविनौ। एवमुत्तमकर्माणौ कुरुवृष्णियशस्करौ॥२८॥
verses.english: Then those two heroes checked each other in that battle which was like a gambling match in which their lives were the stakes. Thus those two enhancers of the glory of the Kuru and the Vrishni races (respectively).

verses.sanskrit: परस्परमयुध्येतां वारणाविव यूथपौ। तावदीर्घेण कालेन ब्रह्मलोकपुरस्कृतौ॥२९॥
verses.english: Fought on with each other like two huge elephants, the leaders of two herds. Those two warriors, both desirous of attaining the highest of regions both longing to attain to the region of Brahma, thus roared at each other. Indeed Satyaki and Somadatta's son continued to cover each with their arrowy downpour in the sight of the delighted Dharatarastras. The people then witnessed that encounter between those two foremost of warriors.

verses.sanskrit: यियासन्तौ परं स्थानमन्योन्यं सञ्जगर्जतुः। सात्यकिः सौमदत्तिश्च शरवृष्ट्या परस्परम्॥३०॥
हृष्टवद्धार्तराष्ट्राणां पश्यतामभ्यवर्षताम्। संप्रैक्षन्त जनास्तौ तु युध्यमानौ युधांपती॥३१॥
यूथपौ वासिताहेतोः प्रयुद्धाविव कुञ्जरौ। अन्योन्यस्य हयान्हत्वा धनुषी विनिकृत्य च॥३२॥
verses.english: Who were fighting like two leaders of elephant herds for the sake of consorting with a she-elephant in her season. Then each slaying the other's steeds and cutting off the other's bow.

verses.sanskrit: विरथावसियुद्धाय समेयातां महारणे। आर्षभे चर्मणी चित्रे प्रगृह्य विपुले शुभे ॥३३॥
verses.english: And thus deprived of the use of their cars, encountered each other for sword fighting. Taking up two large and beautiful and variegated shields made of bull's hide.

verses.sanskrit: विकोशौ चाप्यसी कृत्वा समरे तौ विचेरतुः। चरन्तौ विविधान्मार्गान् मण्डलानि च भागशः॥३४॥
verses.english: And drawing out their swords out of their scabbards, they appeared beautiful on the field of battle. They moved in various motions and described in their montions, various circles.

verses.sanskrit: मुहुराजघ्नतुः क्रुद्धावन्योन्यमरिमर्दनौ। सखड्गौ चित्रवर्माणौ सनिष्काङ्गदभूषणौ॥३५॥
verses.english: Those two subduers of foes incessantly then began to strike one another out of rage. With their swords and covered in variegated coats of mail and adorned with Nikas and Angadas.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रान्तमुद्भ्रान्तमाविद्धमाप्लुतं विप्लुतं सृतम्। संपातं समुदीर्णं च दर्शयन्तौ यशस्विनौ॥३६॥
verses.english: Those two renowned warriors displayed various kinds of motions. They wheeled about and jumped on high, made side thirsts, leapt forward whirled on high, ran and dashed forward and advanced upwards.

verses.sanskrit: असिभ्यां संप्रजह्राते परस्परमरिन्दमौ। उभौ छिद्रैषिणौ वीरावुभौ चित्रं ववल्गतुः॥३७॥
दर्शयन्तावुभौ शिक्षां लाघवं सौष्ठवं तथा। रणे रणकृतां श्रेष्ठावन्योन्यं पर्यकर्षताम्॥३८॥
मुहूर्तमिव राजेन्द्र समाहत्य परस्परम्। पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानां वीरावाश्वसतां पुनः॥३९॥
असिभ्यां चर्मणी चित्रे शतचन्द्रे नराधिप। निकृत्य पुरुषव्याघ्रौ बाहुयुद्धं प्रचक्रतुः॥४०॥
verses.english: Having, with their respective swords cut-off the variegated buckler of each other decked with hundred moons, those foremost of men engaged in a wrestling encounter, O ruler of men.

verses.sanskrit: व्यूढोरस्कौ दीर्घभुजौ नियुद्धकुशलावुभौ। बाहुभिः समसज्जेतामायसैः परिघैरिव॥४१॥
तयो राजन् भुजाघातनिग्रहप्रग्रहास्तथा। शिक्षाबलसमुद्भूताः सर्वयोधप्रहर्षणाः॥४२॥
verses.english: They struck and seized each other with their arms and each seized the others neck with his arms. The skill that hey had acquired by practice, afforded great delight to other warriors who then were turned into mere spectators.

verses.sanskrit: तयोर्नृवरयो राजन्समरे युध्यमानयोः। भीमोऽभवन्महाशब्दो वज्रपर्वतयोरिव॥४३॥
verses.english: The, O king, as those two foremost of men fought on with each other, the sound that then arose, was the like that caused by the striking of thunder against a mountain.
verses.bhavadeepa: भुजाघातो भुजस्फोटः, निग्रहो हस्तधारणं, प्रग्रहो गलहस्तकः ॥४२॥

verses.sanskrit: द्विपाविव विषाणाग्रैः शृङ्गैरिव महर्षभौ। भुजयोक्त्रावबन्धैश्च शिरोभ्यां चावघातनैः॥४४॥
verses.english: Like two elephants fighting with each other with the ends of their tusks, of like two bulls with their horns, those two high-souled and foremost warriors of the Kuru and the Satvata races, fought with each other, sometimes twining each other with their arms, sometimes striking each other with their heads, sometimes binding each other with their legs, sometimes slaping their arm-pits, sometimes scraching each other with their nails, sometimes embracing each other tightly, sometimes twining their legs round each others loins, sometimes rolling on the ground, sometimes going forward and sometime falling back, sometimes challenging each other, sometimes throwing each other down, sometimes rising up and sometimes jumping on high.

verses.sanskrit: पादावकर्षसन्धानैस्तोमरांकुशलासनैः। पादोदरविबन्धैश्च भूमावुद्भ्रमणैस्तथा॥४५॥
गतप्रत्यागताक्षेपैः पातनोत्थानसंप्लुतैः। युयुधाते महात्मानौ कुरुसात्वतपुङ्गवौ॥४६॥
verses.bhavadeepa: पादशब्दः प्रत्येकं सम्बध्यते । पादावकर्षैश्चरणावकर्पणैः, पादसंधानैश्चरणच्छंदितकैः, तोमरैरतिस्फोटनैः, अंकुशैरवलुञ्चनेः, पादोदरविबन्धैः पादाभ्यामुदरक्रोडीकरणैः, उद्भ्रमणैः परिवर्तनैः ॥४५॥

verses.sanskrit: द्वात्रिंशत्करणानि स्युर्यानि युद्धानि भारत। तान्यदर्शयतां तत्र युध्यमानौ महाबलौ॥४७॥
verses.english: Then those two puissant combatant's displayed in that encounter all the thirty kinds of manoeuvres and acts that are the principal feathers of these kinds of encounters.
verses.bhavadeepa: गतैर्गमनैः, प्रत्यागतैरावर्तनैः, आक्षेपैरास्फालनैः, पातनैर्भूमिप्रापणैः, उत्थानैः उत्पतनैः, संप्लुतैः विस्फारानुबन्धैः ॥४६॥

verses.sanskrit: क्षीणायुधे सात्वते युध्यमाने ततोऽब्रवीदर्जुनं वासुदेवः। पश्यस्वैनं विरथं युध्यमानं रणे वरं सर्वधनुर्धराणाम्॥४८॥
verses.english: When during that encounter, the lock of Satwata's weapons was exhausted, Vasudeva's son addressing Arjuna said-" Behold this carless hero, viz., Satyaki, this foremost of all wielder of bow, engaged in fight.

verses.sanskrit: प्रविष्टो भारतीं भित्वा तव पाण्डव पृष्ठतः। योधितश्च महावीर्यैः सर्वैर्भारत भारतैः॥४९॥
verses.english: O son of Pandu, he has followed you having penetrated into the Bharata host. O Bharata, he has fought with many mighty warriors of the Bharata host.

verses.sanskrit: परिश्रान्तं युधां श्रेष्ठं संप्राप्तो भूरिदक्षिणः। युद्धाकांक्षी समायान्तं नैतत्सममिवार्जुन॥५०॥
verses.english: Bhurisravas who has made great sacrificial presents, rushing upon that foremost of warriors viz., Satyaki exhausted with fatigue, has no encountered him. This is indeed very unfair."

verses.sanskrit: ततो भूरिश्रवाः क्रुद्धः सात्यकिं युद्धदुर्मदः। उद्यम्याभ्यहनद्राजन्मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम्॥५१॥
verses.english: Then the indomitable Bhurisravas inflamed with rage, uplifting his sword struck Satyaki like a mad elephant striking another in the same state.

verses.sanskrit: रथस्थयोर्द्वयोर्युद्धे क्रुद्धयोर्योधमुख्ययोः। केशवार्जुनयो राजन्समरे प्रेक्षमाणयोः॥५२॥
अथ कृष्णो महाबाहुरर्जुनं प्रत्यभाषत। पश्य वृष्ण्यन्धकव्याघ्रं सौमदत्तिवशं गतम्॥५३॥
परिभ्रान्तं गतं भूमौ कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। तवान्तेवासिनं वीरं पालयार्जुन सात्यकिम्॥५४॥
न वशं यज्ञशीलस्य गच्छेदेष वरोऽर्जुन। त्वत्कृते पुरुषव्याघ्र तदाशु क्रियतां विभो॥५५॥
verses.english: O foremost of men, O Arjuna, do you soon take that measure by which Satyaki many not succumb to Bhurisravas the performer of numerous sacrifices, O lord.”

verses.sanskrit: अथाब्रवीद्धृष्टमना वासुदेवं धनञ्जयः। पश्य वृष्णिप्रवीरेण क्रीडन्तं कुरुपुङ्गवम्॥५६॥

महाद्विपेनेव वने मत्तेन हरियूथपम्।
              सञ्जय उवाच।
              इत्येवं भाषमाणे तु पाण्डवे वै धनञ्जये ॥५७॥
verses.english: Like a huge and infuriate elephant sporting in the woods with mighty lion.” While Pandu's son Dhananjaya was thus speaking.

verses.sanskrit: हाहाकारो महानासीत्सैन्यानां भरतर्षभ। तदुद्यम्य महाबाहुः सात्यकिं न्यहनद्भुवि॥५८॥
verses.english: Loud cried of Oh and Alas arose among the troops, foremost of the Bharatas, as the mighty-armed (Bhurisravas) striking vigorously had brought Satyaki down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit: स सिंह इव मातङ्गं विकर्षन् भूरिदक्षिणः। व्यरोचत कुरुश्रेष्ठः सात्वतप्रवरं युधि॥५९॥
verses.english: Then like a lion dragging an elephant, that foremost of the Kuru race, namely Bhurisravas, that destroyer of darkness, looked beautiful in that battle as he dragged that foremost one of the Satwatas.

verses.sanskrit: अथ कोशाद्विनिष्कृष्य खड्गं भूरिश्रवा रणे। मूर्धजेषु निजग्राह पदा चोरस्यताडयत्॥६०॥
ततोऽस्य छेत्तुमारब्धः शिरः कायात्सकुण्डलम्। तावत्क्षणात्सात्वतोऽपि शिरः संभ्रमयंस्त्वरन्॥६१॥
verses.english: Bhurisravas was then about to sever from Satyaki's trunk his head graced with earrings. For sometimes, that hero of the Satvata race rapidly whirling round with the rod.

verses.sanskrit: यथा चक्रं तु कौलालो दण्डविद्धं तु भारत। सहैव भूरिश्रवसो बाहुना केशधारिणा॥६२॥
verses.english: Together with the arm of Bhurisravas that held it by the hair, like a potters wheel whirling round with the rod.

verses.sanskrit: तं तथा परिकृष्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा सात्वतमाहवे। वासुदेवस्ततो राजन्भूयोऽर्जुनमभाषत॥६३॥
verses.english: Beholding the Satvata hero thus dragged by Bhurisravas, Vasudeva once more addressing Arjuna said-

verses.sanskrit: पश्य वृष्ण्यन्धकव्याघ्रं सौमदत्तिवशं गतम्। तव शिष्यं महाबाहो धनुष्यनवरं त्वया॥६४॥
verses.english: Behold O mighty-armed one, that foremost hero among the Vrishnis and Andhakas, that disciple of yours who is not inferior to you in bowmanship, succumb to the son of Somadatta.

verses.sanskrit: असत्यो विक्रमः पार्थ यत्र भूरिश्रवा रणे। विशेषयति वार्ष्णेयं सात्यकिं सत्यविक्रमम्॥६५॥
verses.english: Behold, O son of Partha, the weak Bhurisravas obtain advantage over the Vrishni hero Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तो महाबाहुर्वासुदेवेन पाण्डवः। मनसा पूजयामास भूरिश्रवसमाहवे॥६६॥
verses.english: The mighty-armed son of Pandu thus spoken to by Vasudeva (Krishna), worshipped Bhurisravas in his minds.

verses.sanskrit: विकर्षन्सात्वतश्रेष्ठं क्रीडमान इवाहवे। संहर्षयति मां भूयः कुरूणां कीर्तिवर्धनः॥६७॥
प्रवरं वृष्णिवीराणां यन्न हन्याद्धि सात्यकिम्। महाद्विपमिवारण्ये मृगेन्द्र इव कर्षति॥६८॥
एवं तु मनसा राजन्पार्थः संपूज्य कौरवम्। वासुदेवं महाबाहुरर्जुनः प्रत्यभाषत॥६९॥
verses.bhavadeepa: न हन्याद्धन्तुं न शक्नोति द्वितीय इव शब्द एवार्थे कर्षत्येवेत्यन्वयः ॥६८॥

verses.sanskrit: सैन्धवे सक्तदृष्टित्वान्नैनं पश्यामि माधवम्। एतत्त्वसुकरं कर्म यादवार्थे करोम्यहम् ॥७०॥
verses.english: “O Madhava, my eyes being fixed on the ruler of the Sindhus, I cannot see Bhurisravas; but for the sake of that descendant of Yadu's, race, I shall perform a very difficult feat.”

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा वचनं कुर्वन्वासुदेवस्य पाण्डवः। ततः क्षुरप्रं निशितं गाण्डीवे समयोजयत्॥७१॥
पार्थबाहुविसृष्टः स महोल्केव नभश्च्युता। सखड्गं यज्ञशीलस्य साङ्गदं बाहुमच्छिनत्॥७२॥
verses.english: That arrow shot by the force of Partha's arms and looking like a meteor dropping from the skies, cut-off the arm of that one devoted to the performance of sacrifice arm that was decked with Angadas and had a sword in its grasp.
